steps.title: Complete Your Brand Profile
steps.text: In Settings → Profile → Brand & AI Profile, add your name, brokerage, phones, website, and license number. Upload your logo and your headshot — the headshot becomes your AI Photo Avatar, and your contact card and logo appear automatically in every video.

steps.title: Set Your Market
steps.text: In Settings → Profile → Content Preferences, enter your city, state, and video language. This powers live local market research, trending topics, and auto-localized templates.

steps.title: Create Your AI Voice
steps.text:
In Settings → Profile → AI Voice Clone, record or upload about 30 seconds of your voice. Your AI videos will speak in your voice.
The card has two tabs. Record my voice gives you a short script to read aloud, which you can edit or replace with your own words. Press Start recording, speak clearly and naturally for at least 30 seconds, press Stop Recording, then Use this recording, or Re-record to try again. Upload a file is for a recording you already have.
If your voice clone ever stops being available, a video tells you before it is made and nothing is taken from your plan. Record your voice again here and try again.

steps.title: Set Your Default Video CTA
steps.text: In Settings → Profile → Default Video CTA, add your years in real estate and review the pre-written closing call-to-action. It auto-fills your name, team, and each video's city — edit it once and every video ends with a proven subscribe-and-contact close. Change it later and it carries into videos you have already started, unless you typed over the closing line in that video; Use my saved CTA there brings it back.

steps.title: Connect YouTube And Your Other Accounts
steps.text:
In Settings → Social Accounts, connect the Google account that owns your channel. One-time tip: verify the channel by phone at youtube.com/verify so your thumbnails are added automatically.
Still not working? YouTube's verify page opens for whichever channel your browser is on, so check the picture at its top right is this channel. If it isn't, open the page in a private window signed in to this channel only. And one phone number verifies two channels a year: if YouTube says yours is used up, use another phone or a landline.
On a paid plan the same screen has More platforms: Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, TikTok, X, Threads and Google Business. Press Connect beside each one you use and approve it on that platform's own screen, which names Upload-Post, the service that delivers your posts. Connect as many as you like, and Disconnect any of them there too. A few need the right kind of account: Instagram must be a Business or Creator account linked to a Facebook Page, Facebook must be a Page rather than your personal profile, and Google Business must be a verified profile.
If an account can post to more than one place, a Posts to choice appears under it: which Facebook Page, your LinkedIn profile or a company page, which Google Business location. Pick once and every post goes there. With two Facebook Pages or two locations you do have to pick, or posts there won't go out.
BoldTrail. If you use BoldTrail, SparkReels can email your sellers and clients through it, from your own BoldTrail address, and BoldTrail keeps each email on that contact's record. In BoldTrail, go to Lead Engine → Lead Dropbox → My API Tokens, tick Contacts, press Generate and copy the token. Then paste it into the BoldTrail box in Settings → CRM Integration and press Connect. It's saved securely and shown only by its last four characters; Disconnect removes it. If BoldTrail won't send with a Contacts token, make one with All ticked. Tokens last a year.

steps.title: Save Your Import Address
steps.text:
In Settings → Profile → Import Articles By Email you have a private address that looks like yourname-k7m3qz@in.sparkreels.ai. Forward anything to it — a newsletter, a market report, an article someone sent you, or a post you wrote yourself — and it appears inside SparkReels within a minute, with the signatures, forwarding headers and unsubscribe footers already stripped out. Press Email this address to me and save it to your contacts; after that, forwarding is the whole of it.
It is private to your account, so treat it like a password. Anyone who has it can send articles into your list, and you can replace it any time from the same screen.
Once something has arrived, Spark Studio has it under My Content/Forwarded in, in the Script source row, with a new badge when something has come in since you last looked. Open it, choose From email, and pick the one you want. Nothing is written until you press the button at the bottom of the page. The whole piece is read, up to about 10,000 words, so a long market report is used to its last page. Forwarded emails are kept for 30 days.

steps.title: Start With The Topic, Then Choose What To Make
steps.text:
Spark Studio has four sections, top to bottom. 1 · Say or Pick a Topic — one card with the mic and a box, where you say or type what it's about (step 8). 2 · Create — four cards: Video / Reel, Camera/Teleprompter, Blog or Listings & photos. Video / Reel stays on this page; the other three each open a page of their own, with Back on the bar at the bottom to return here. A topic you already said or typed comes with you. 3 · Script Source — AI writes it from a topic, or My Content/Forwarded in, which is also where anything you forwarded in turns up (step 6). A listing or a photos only reel skips this one (step 13). 4 · Details — the city and state, who it's for, and a video's format.
You don't have to work down all four. Give it a topic at the top, check the city and state, and press Next at the bottom. The sections underneath are there for when you want to change something first.
Video / Reel is three kinds of video, and they sit right under that card for you to pick, so the script is written to suit. Pick one any time; if you press Next first, they light up and ask. Avatar video puts you on screen with b-roll and graphics made for you. Avatar in circle puts you in a corner circle over scenes that follow what you're saying. Voice over only has nobody on screen: it is a Scenes Reel (step 11). Each uses one short video. If your sentence already said which, such as “with my avatar” or “voice over only”, it isn't asked.
Whatever you pick, it starts a Spark — the folder holding that topic's script, its videos, its article and where they've been published. It's created the moment you begin, so an idea saved and left half-finished is still there marked Draft, not lost. Part 5 explains where Sparks live and how they differ from the videos themselves.
Already written it? My Content/Forwarded in is the one place for it, the second box under Script source. Paste your words in, or attach a PDF, a link, or an email you forwarded to your import address (step 6). On a video you then say what happens to them: Speak it word for word, for a finished script, or Have AI write from it, which either writes a new script from it or shortens an article of your own. The script comes back for you to read before anything is made. If an email's subject names a town, the city and state fill in for you. Recording yourself has its own version of this, From a document.
On the Blog page the same tile is there, and you choose what happens to it: Use it as it is, which publishes your words unchanged and takes seconds, or Write a new article from it, which covers the same ground in your voice for your market. Use the first for your own writing and the second for someone else's — a newsletter another person wrote is theirs, not yours to publish. A market report is the second kind: it is a data provider's pages of listings, so have a new article written from it rather than publishing it as it stands.
Who is it for? Audience, Tone and Why are three optional pickers under Details. What you choose shapes the script, the article and the Spark Tools afterwards. You can also just say them: “for first-time buyers”, “make it vertical”. If your audience is not on the list — first responders, nurses relocating — choose Add your own… at the bottom of Audience and type it. It is saved to your account, so it is there on your phone and your computer, and choosing it again shows Remove from my list for when you no longer want it.

steps.title: Speak It Or Type It — Your Choice
steps.text:
Need help on a section? Tap Sparklee, the gold star at the top of the screen, or Ask Sparklee at the end of the steps on Spark Studio, and ask out loud how to do something. She answers in a few seconds, out loud and on screen, from this guide. Each conversation runs up to five minutes. Five conversations a day before you pick a plan, twenty a day on one. The Topic card at the top of Spark Studio reads Say it in your own words. It has one mic and one box, and they are the same thing: what you say shows up in the box, and what you type goes in the same place. Tap the mic and say the whole thing in one sentence — “Create a blog for downsizers about one-floor living in Springfield” or “Make a vertical video with my avatar about the Riverside market” — and tap the mic again when you're done. Your words stay in the box, so a misheard town or street name is a quick fix.
A moment after you stop, the page fills itself in from what you said: the card under 2 · Create lights up, the city and state appear under 4 · Details, and the audience and format are set if you named them. Look down the page to check it, change anything by hand, and press Next at the bottom. Say more and it is added to the box and read again. Say “Spark it” and it presses Next for you.
A blog is written straight away. A video stops at its script, so nothing comes out of your plan until you choose to make it. The script's length follows the format: up to 90 seconds for Vertical, up to 3 minutes for Horizontal, and up to 8 minutes for Longform.
Say “make a reel about…” and it makes a Voice over only Scenes Reel (step 11). Say who's in it, as in “a reel with my avatar”, and it makes that instead.
The cards follow along. Say “create a blog” and the Blog card is the one picked; tap a card yourself and the box makes that instead.
You can start from an email you forwarded the same way: “Create a blog from my Springfield market report email.” It only looks through your emails when you say “email” or “forwarded”, so “a market update for Springfield” still means a fresh one.
You don't have to say it all at once. Give it the topic, then the town, then who it's for, one answer at a time, and it keeps what it has already heard. On a desktop you can hold Spacebar anywhere on the page instead of tapping the mic. Once it says it has everything, saying “Spark it” starts it too.
Prefer typing, or want a suggestion instead of a blank box? The box shows a Try example that changes every few seconds; press the empty box to use the one showing, or just start typing. Under it is a Quick win: a ready topic for your town in one press, with a new idea each time you sign in (your very first one is a market update). Then What buyers ask AI (step 19), and under that Or try: ideas with your city filled in, with More ideas opening the whole list and a search box. Tap one and it lands in the same box the mic writes into, so you can add to it before you send. Either way, AI researches live market data for your city and writes a broadcast-quality script with real stats.

steps.title: Review & Edit The Script
steps.text: Pick your favorite hook — it becomes the video title too, so the two never disagree. Edit the script freely; a live word counter keeps you inside the cap. Your Call To Action is on the next screen, in Video setup under Music: it is spoken after your script, so edit it there, or tick No call to action to end the video on your script. Regenerate redoes it from the same topic — it asks first, since it discards your edits.

steps.title: Choose Format And Who's On Screen — Then Generate
steps.text:
Pick a format: Vertical 9:16 for Reels, Shorts and TikTok, or Horizontal 16:9 for YouTube and websites — both up to 3 minutes — or Longform 16:9 (up to 8 minutes, using your own photos for visuals; long videos have their own monthly allowance — 2 with Producer, 4 with Influencer — or $49 on its own).
Then who's on screen, four choices that are the same for every script, whether AI wrote it or you pasted your own:
Avatar video — you on screen, with b-roll and graphics made for you. Up to 3 minutes, so it is not offered for Longform. It takes a script of up to 400 words, counting your closing line. If yours is longer, Avatar video is greyed out and a note under the choices says how many words you have. Press Shorten to fit and the script is cut to fit, or Shorten closing line to trim your closing line yourself.
Avatar in circle — you in a corner circle, speaking the script exactly as written, over scenes made for each sentence. Attach a few photos and each takes a sentence among the scenes; attach many and the photos are the background.
Voice over only — nobody on screen. Your voice over AI scenes made for each sentence, or over your photos if you attached some. The quickest of the three.
You on camera — the free way out of this screen. It hands your script and photos to the camera instead of making a video.
The first three use one video from your plan. Attach photos or documents as b-roll, and hit Spark Video. How long it takes follows the length of the script, not the format: Voice over only is usually ready in 2 to 10 minutes, an avatar video in 5 to 20, and a long one can take up to an hour. You can close the page and watch for it in My Sparks. If a video fails, your allowance is refunded automatically. When lots of videos are being made at once, yours waits in line and starts on its own a few minutes later; nothing is charged until it starts.

steps.title: Voice Over Only — The Scenes Reel
steps.text:
A Scenes Reel needs no photos, no camera and no face. Your voice clone reads the script over short, realistic scenes made with AI, one for each sentence, on screen while that sentence is spoken. It is the quickest video to make and a good fit for Reels and Shorts.
To make one: give the Topic card a topic, choose Video / Reel, pick Voice over only under it, and press Next. Or just say “make a reel about winter selling tips in Springfield”.
The script is written for you and waits to be read. Edit it, or tap Rewrite. Choose a length — 30 sec, 60 sec, 90 sec, 2 min or 3 min — Vertical or Horizontal, captions, music and your closing card, then press Build the Scenes reel.
It builds on its own after that, so you can leave the page. It shows as rendering in My Sparks and then as finished: a few minutes for a short one, around ten for three minutes. If it can't be built, My Sparks says so and nothing is taken from your plan.
The scenes show what each sentence is about and change from one to the next: close-ups, rooms, streets, different light. They are generic on purpose. People appear only from behind or at a distance, there are no readable words, and it is never your town or a real listing. For a real property use a Photos only reel with its own photos (step 13). A Scenes Reel uses one short video, and “Scenes made with AI.” is added to its description.

steps.title: Camera/Teleprompter — The Free Option
steps.text:
Pressing Camera/Teleprompter opens a page of its own, with Back on the bar at the bottom to return to Spark Studio. On a computer it starts with Record yourself or Record your screen. What we're writing comes next — your market, how long the script should be, and where the words come from: a topic, a PDF or link, a recording of you talking, your own typing, or Speak naturally, which is no script and no teleprompter at all. When AI is writing it from a topic, the mic box at the top of this page holds the topic — anything you already said or typed on Spark Studio comes with you — and Write my script in the bar at the bottom writes it and loads it into your teleprompter. Then how it records — vertical or horizontal, Branded Look, what plays behind you, and Add Channel CTA to append your closing pitch. You can also skip straight here with Record on Camera, a one-click button on any script or blog post. The teleprompter scrolls automatically while you record in up to 1080p/60fps, for up to 15 minutes (8–15 min is YouTube's algorithm sweet spot and unlocks mid-roll ads). On a computer, press Camera/Teleprompter and choose Record your screen to record a listing, a market report or anything else on screen while you talk, with you in a corner circle or not. It records horizontal, up to 10 minutes, and finishes like any camera recording.
What plays behind you is one of three things, with you in the corner. Your photos, if you attached any. Play my footage behind me, a clip of your own. Or, with neither, Make scenes from my script: short realistic scenes made with AI, one for each part of what you're about to say, in order. People appear only from behind or at a distance, and it is never your town or a real property. Scenes take about three minutes to make and use one short video from your plan; photos and your own footage stay free. Write the script first, because the scenes are made from it.
With a clip or scenes chosen you can tick Open on it. The first 5 seconds of the take are then the clip full screen with a title you type, and you appear after that. Start talking as soon as you press record; your voice is heard over the opener.
If the upload doesn't go through, the take is kept on this device rather than lost. You'll see “Your recording is safely waiting on this device” with Retry Upload and Download. Retrying is always safe: it checks whether the recording already reached us rather than saving a second copy, so a lost reply can never turn into two videos. Download first if you want your own copy before leaving the page.

steps.title: Listings And Photos Only Reels
steps.text:
Listings & photos, the fourth card, opens a page of its own with two tabs, and both start from a set of property pictures. Back, on the bar at the bottom, returns to Spark Studio. Listing video writes a tour from the listing — paste a listing link, upload photos or enter the details — and renders it in your voice, with your avatar on screen or the photos full-frame. It uses one short video. Once the address and price are in, press Next · video setup on the bar at the bottom to have the tour written, or Write it — I'll read it on camera to go straight to the teleprompter with your photos behind you, free.
Photos only reel needs no script at all. Add up to 12 photos — upload them, or paste a listing link and its photos are brought in for you — then pick the format ( Vertical or Horizontal ), a length, music, and whether it has a voiceover and a closing card with your ask and phone number. A voiceover you type is read in your own voice clone once you have set one up, and by a stock voice until then. Then choose the Motion:
Classic is a slow pan across each photo. It is free and takes nothing from your plan.
Cinematic turns each photo into a few seconds of gentle camera movement, and uses one short video. It takes up to 8 photos and 60 seconds, and works best on rooms and exteriors — avoid photos with people in them, because they can come out looking different. Every clip is checked against its photo; one that drifts away from it is dropped and that photo gets the classic pan instead. If fewer than half your photos can be animated, no video is taken from your plan. “Photos animated with AI.” is added to the description, so the reel says what it is.
Build the reel is on the bar at the bottom. When the reel is done it becomes View your reel. Make another reel, at the foot of the form, brings the build button back — on Cinematic that is another short video.
Post these photos, at the foot of the form, sends the same photos as they are: one post to swipe through on Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, Threads, X or TikTok. No video is made and nothing comes out of your plan. Pick the accounts, write one caption for the post, and send. The order you arranged them in is the swipe order. Instagram takes the first ten, and trims a very tall or very wide photo to a shape it accepts.
No photos to start from? That is a Scenes Reel (step 11).

steps.title: Your Share Kit — And A Blog Post
steps.text:
Every video finishes on its Share Kit: the title, description and hashtags Publish fills in for you, plus an Instagram caption, a LinkedIn post and an email blurb. It also holds a blog article — usually 1,000 to 1,500 words, titled with the question a reader would actually type, headings written the same way and answered in the first line, and a Frequently Asked Questions section of six questions at the end, chosen from what people are asking about that subject in your town. Those six are AI answer blocks, built into every article (step 19). That is the shape an AI assistant quotes — AEO and GEO, alongside ordinary SEO. Header image makes the picture that sits above the headline — a real photograph of the kind of place the article is about, with no words drawn into it — and Copy as HTML then carries it across with the text, so what you paste into your site arrives with its image already in place. The same paste includes the article's schema, the hidden description that tells search and answer engines what the article is, who wrote it, and which parts are questions and answers. Some website builders remove it when you paste; the article is unaffected. Once an article has a header image, two more buttons appear beside it. Moving header turns that picture into a short silent loop of slow camera movement, and Copy as HTML then leads with it, keeping the still picture for sites that won't play video. Social teaser makes a short vertical clip with the headline and a “Read the full article” card, to download and post with a link. Each takes about a minute, neither uses a video from your plan, and each can be made up to four times for one article. That gives one recording two places to be quoted from: the video's own description, which is written with a real FAQ block for voice search, and the article on your own site. Blog posts never use a video from your plan, and you can write one without making a video at all — press the Blog card, which opens a page of its own with the mic box, Source and Details and Back on the bar at the bottom, or start your sentence with “create a blog”.
Posting it on your BoldTrail website. Press Copy as HTML. In BoldTrail, open your website (WebIDX), go to Blog and press Add Post. In the editor, click the <> button to open the code view, paste, and press Save. Give the post its title (use the Headline from your Share Kit), then Publish. Once it's live, open the post, copy its web address from your browser's address bar, and paste it into the email's link box, so Read more in your emails and newsletters goes straight to it.
Coming from a camera recording or a pasted script, the article starts writing itself as soon as the Share Kit opens — there is nothing to press. A take recorded with no script still has a Write the article button, because the words have to be taken off the video first. Before your free video it also waits for the button, so it never uses one of your free tries without being asked.
Email, in the article's row of buttons, turns the article into an email for your list: a short version with a button through to the full post. Paste in the address of the post on your site and the button points there. Send me a test sends it to the address you sign in with, so you can see it in a real inbox (look in spam the first time), and Copy as HTML drops it into the email tool you already use. With BoldTrail connected, Send through BoldTrail under the preview sends it to up to 10 people from your BoldTrail address, each greeted by their first name, once the post's web address is in. Without BoldTrail, SparkReels doesn't send it to your clients for you.
A newsletter from several posts. In My Sparks, press Make a newsletter above your Blog posts, tick 2 to 5 of them, then Make the newsletter. It writes three subject lines, the inbox preview, a short note from you, a few lines on each post with its own Read more button, and your sign-off. Paste each post's web address once; a post without one has no button. Copy as HTML drops it into the email tool you already use, and Send me a test sends it to you first. With BoldTrail connected, it can go to up to 10 people from there too, once every post's web address is in. Without BoldTrail, SparkReels doesn't send it to your clients for you.

steps.title: Publish To YouTube — One Click
steps.text:
Open the finished video in My Sparks and hit Publish. Your AI-generated title, description, and hashtags are attached automatically — choose public, unlisted, or private, and you're live without leaving the app. Avatar videos, Cinematic reels, Scenes reels and a camera recording made over AI scenes are marked to YouTube as AI-made when they go up, which YouTube asks for. Other videos you record yourself and Classic reels are not.
If a publish fails — an expired YouTube connection, a channel limit, a video still finishing — it isn't lost in a disappearing message. Open Publish on that video again: the top of the window lists where it has gone, and a failed one shows the reason with a Retry beside it. Once a later attempt goes through, the line reads as posted.
If YouTube needs reconnecting, which happens when Google ends the connection on its side, Publish says so and shows a Reconnect YouTube link. Your channel is remembered; reconnect and publish again.

steps.title: Everywhere Else — From The Same Window
steps.text:
The Publish window lists every account you connected in step 5. Tick the ones this video should go to and the button names them — Publish to Facebook, Publish to YouTube and Instagram. Nothing goes out until you press it. Creator posts each video to YouTube plus three others; Producer and Influencer post to all of them.
Caption / Post Text appears as soon as you tick anything besides YouTube. It starts with the caption and hashtags written for the video, and what you leave there is what gets posted.
First comment is optional, and is posted under the video on Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, Threads and TikTok. It is the place for a link, because a link in an Instagram caption can't be clicked and one in a comment can. If you saved your blog post's address for this video, it is already filled in.
YouTube is live the moment it finishes. The others take a few minutes to process the video, so the window says On its way and tells you as each one lands, or why one did not. You can close it; the post carries on either way.
Where it's posted, at the top of the window, is the record for that video: one line for each platform, saying posted (with a link to the post), on its way, scheduled, or failed and why. A failed line has Retry, which sends the video to that one platform again. A posted line on Facebook or LinkedIn has Edit caption, for fixing the words after it is up; the other platforms don't allow that. Platforms the video is already on start unticked when you reopen the window, so it isn't posted to them twice by accident.
If a post doesn't go out after you've left the window, you are told two ways. A red note appears at the top of My Sparks naming the platform, the video and the reason, with Open Publish to go straight to Retry and Dismiss to clear it. And an email goes to the address you sign in with. The usual reason is a connection that has expired and needs connecting again in Settings.
The thumbnail you set in the window is sent with the video as its cover, not only to YouTube. A vertical video gets a tall version of the same thumbnail. Each platform decides whether to show it; some pick a frame of their own.
Google Business works differently. It takes no more than 30 seconds of video and no phone numbers, so a longer video goes up as a photo post with your caption, any phone number left out, and a Learn more button to your blog post or the video. A long caption is trimmed to fit Google's limit. A video too long for one of the other platforms is skipped there, with the reason shown.
For an open house, tick Post to Google as an event and give it a name, the date and the start and end times. Google shows the date on your listing and takes the post down by itself afterwards, where an ordinary post would still say “this Saturday” a week later.
For anywhere you have not connected, download the MP4 and use the pre-written Instagram caption, LinkedIn post, and email blurb from the project's Title, Description & Hashtags card.
Email it. Any finished video in My Sparks can be emailed. Press Email it, add up to 10 people from your BoldTrail by their email (people you've sent a video to before, and your sellers, are one tap), and SparkReels writes a short subject and note that you can change or say out loud. Put {" "} in the note and each person sees their own name. The email shows a picture from the video with a play button and a Watch the video button; email can't play a video inside the message, so a tap opens it. Send through BoldTrail asks you to confirm, then each person gets their own email from your BoldTrail address. Without BoldTrail, copy it into your own email instead. For your whole list, use your email tool or BoldTrail's own campaigns, which handle unsubscribes.

steps.title: The Everyday Tools
steps.text:
You don't need Spark Tools to make a video — Spark Studio generates everything automatically. Use these to iterate: brainstorm 8 title angles before committing, draft and compare scripts without creating projects, regenerate a description or 20 fresh tags for any video (including older ones), and name your channel (one-time). LinkedIn Profile is one-time too: it writes your headline, About, current position, top skills, custom URL and a post announcing your channel, each with where to paste it, and can write a Company Page for your team. From any project's Title, Description & Hashtags card, tap “Improve With AI Tools” and it opens the right tool with that project already loaded.
Google Reviews shows the reviews on your Google Business profile, with your average and how many there are. It needs Google Business connected (step 5). Needs a reply is ticked to begin with, so you see only the ones you haven't answered; untick it to see them all. On any review, Draft a reply writes a short one in your voice for you to edit, or Write my own gives you an empty box. Nothing goes to Google until you press Post reply. A reply you've already posted can be edited or removed. Read a drafted reply to a low rating with extra care before posting it.
Seller Update writes an update email to the people selling one of your listings, whenever you want to send one. Add the listing once: the address, the sellers' first names, the list price and the date it was listed. If you've already made a video or reel of it in Listings & photos, pick it under From your listings and the address fills in. For each update, fill in online views, saves, showings, open house visitors and offers, and type or say the buyer feedback and next steps. Your last update's numbers show beside each box, and the email shows the new ones as a row of numbers with what went up. It uses only what you enter. Past updates are listed under the listing. Record a video update writes a short script from your numbers and opens the camera with it; when you've recorded, Add to the seller update puts the video at the top of the email, where sellers tap it to watch. Your listings also sit under Seller updates in My Sparks, each with a New update button. With BoldTrail connected, add the sellers by their email under Sellers in BoldTrail, once per listing, and Send to sellers through BoldTrail emails each of them the update, video included, after you confirm, with an optional short text to say it's on its way. The update then shows when it was sent and to whom. Copy it or send yourself a test, the same as the newsletter.

steps.title: Graphics Without A Designer
steps.text:
The Image Generator makes a finished graphic: pick Just listed, Open house, Market update, Blog header or Blank, describe the picture you want, and type your own headline. The photograph is generated; your words are drawn as real type on top, never by the AI — so a price or an address is always spelled right. Choose 4:5 for Instagram and Facebook, 9:16 for Stories and Reels, or 16:9 for a blog or YouTube, and it carries your logo and headshot.
Each press makes one AI photo and counts one against your monthly allowance of 100. Update text redraws your words on the same picture and costs nothing, and using My photo or one of your listing photos is free. New background makes another photo, and counts as one. Use as blog header sends it straight to the article it belongs to. Post it sends the finished graphic to your connected accounts as a photo post, with a caption you write, instead of downloading it first.
The Thumbnail Generator makes the cover picture for a video. Pick the video, type the few words you want on it or leave that blank and AI writes them, and choose the photo. Afterwards you can change the words or the photo and press Update Thumbnail, which redraws it in seconds on the same background. The Market Badge is the city and state shown on it. Type a different one to change it, which also updates the video's market so its title and description match, or clear both boxes and press Update Thumbnail to leave the badge off.
Banners makes the wide image across the top of your YouTube channel, your LinkedIn profile or your Facebook page, each at the size that site wants. Put your photo on the left or the right, pick a color palette or choose Custom and set your own colors, and add QR codes to your site. Download the picture, or use Download for Canva (PDF) for a copy meant to be opened in Canva, where you can change the text and colors yourself.

steps.title: AI Answer Blocks — Get Cited By AI Search
steps.text:
Buyers ask ChatGPT and Perplexity things like “which neighborhood should I buy in?” months before they call an agent. On Create, under the topic box, What buyers ask AI shows a question buyers in your city are asking right now, using the city in Settings unless you type another in Details. Show more opens the rest, and Record this makes one your topic, so the video answers it.
Every blog article already has answer blocks. The six questions at the end of each article in your Share Kit (step 14) are written the way AI assistants quote, for that article's topic, so there is nothing extra to make.
The full tool is the first tab in Spark Tools. For each question it also gives a ready-to-paste block for your website and a Record on Camera shortcut straight to the teleprompter.

steps.title: What A Spark Is
steps.text:
A Spark is one idea and everything that came out of it: the script, the video or videos made from it, the article, the captions, and where each has been published. One topic, one Spark — even if you make a short version, a long version and a reel from it.
Two places in the menu use the word, and they hold different things. My Sparks is your library: the finished videos and drafts themselves, to watch, download, publish or delete. The All Sparks panel inside Spark Calendar lists the Sparks — open one and you get its card, holding the article, the captions, the schedule and how it's performing.

steps.title: Spark Insights — What You Have And How It Did
steps.text:
Spark Insights opens with what you have left — short videos, long videos, and whether camera recording is unlocked with the days remaining — a Getting Started checklist that disappears once you've finished it, and buttons to create a video or open the calendar. Your five most recent projects are at the bottom to pick back up.
Then it looks backwards. How many videos you've made and published, a breakdown by platform and by video shape, and — for anything published to your connected YouTube channel — real views, likes and comments, with every video ranked and linked. Those numbers are fetched from YouTube once a day, so they're yesterday's picture rather than live, and they only cover videos published from September onwards. The same figures appear on each Spark's own card, counting just that Spark's videos.
Watch time and click-through aren't there yet — YouTube keeps those behind a separate permission. Views, likes and comments are what a connected channel gives us today.

steps.title: Spark Calendar — When It Goes Out
steps.text: The calendar puts every dated item — published or scheduled — on a month, week or list view, with the All Sparks panel beside it for everything that has no date yet. Open any Spark from either side to reach its card. This one is still rolling out: it appears in your menu when your account has it.

parts.title: Getting Around
parts.text:
The menu runs across the top on a computer: Spark Studio, My Sparks, Spark Tools, Spark Calendar, Spark Insights, Affiliate, Settings and How It Works. The page you are on is underlined. On a smaller window the last few are under More; on a phone, tap ☰.
Settings has three tabs. Profile holds your brand, market, voice, closing call to action, import address and password. Social Accounts is where YouTube and your other platforms are connected. Billing is your plan and buying more videos.
Your initial, at the top right, opens your email, your plan and Sign Out.
Sparklee, the gold star beside it, answers out loud when you ask how to do something on the page you are on. Tap her to start, and tap Stop when you're done.
Put SparkReels on your phone's Home Screen so it opens like an app. On an iPhone, open sparkreels.ai in Safari, tap the Share button (the square with an arrow), then Add to Home Screen. On Android, open it in Chrome, tap the ⋮ menu, then Add to Home screen (or Install app ).
The first time you sign in, Sparklee asks you to set up your profile. Ask me how has her talk you through it; Go to Settings takes you straight there.

parts.title: Ways To Create
parts.text:
Mode | Best For | Cost
Camera/Teleprompter | Film yourself with the teleprompter | FREE, unlimited*
Blog | Words for your own site — no video made at all | FREE, unlimited*
Avatar video | You on screen, with b-roll and graphics made for you. Up to 3 minutes | 1 short video
Avatar in circle | You in a corner circle, over AI scenes that follow each sentence, with your photos among them | 1 short video
Voice over only | A Scenes Reel: no face, no photos, no camera. Your voice over AI scenes, up to 3 minutes | 1 short video
My Content/Forwarded in | A finished script spoken exactly as written — or an article, a PDF, a link or a forwarded email that AI writes from | FREE as a blog*
1 short video as a video
Listing video | A scripted tour, written from the listing | 1 short video
Photos only reel · Classic | Your photos with a slow pan across each, and music or your voice | FREE
Photos only reel · Cinematic | Each photo becomes a few seconds of real camera movement | 1 short video
* Unlimited on any paid plan. On the free 100-agent beta, camera recording, blog posts and every AI Tool are unlimited for 30 days starting the day you generate your free video. Before that video, you get 1 free blog, 1 free camera recording, 2 free tries of the AI Tools and 2 free AI images to see how they work — one try per tool run. Making the video is free and lifts all of those limits.

parts.title: Get It In Front Of People
The Weekly Rhythm
parts.text:
Once: set up your profile, voice, avatar, CTA, YouTube and your email import address (Part 1)
Weekly: hit the mic and say it, tap a topic chip, or forward a report → generate script → Spark Video — about 5 minutes of your time
Publish: one window sends it to YouTube and the other accounts you connected, with title, description, and tags attached
For a listing: a Classic photos only reel is free; Cinematic or a listing video uses one short video
No photos and no camera: Voice over only makes a Scenes Reel from a topic, up to 3 minutes, for one short video
Mix in free camera videos — YouTube's algorithm loves 8–15 minute authentic long-form
Every one also gives you a blog article for your own site, which costs nothing from your plan
Part 5 covers Sparks and Spark Insights — where your work lives and how it's doing. The Spark Calendar described there is still rolling out, and appears in your menu when your account has it.
